_doc: Progress entries, newest first. 'status' is one of: demonstrated, in-progress, goal. Set 'published' to false to keep a slot in the file without rendering it. 'media' is null or {type: 'video'|'image', src, poster (video), alt, width, height}. Every entry needs a caption-quality 'text' and an 'attribution'. 'gallery.items' are lighter entries for the grid at the end of the section: {title, tag, caption, attribution, media}.
intro: What has been built so far, with honest status labels. Entries are added as results are documented; every photo or video carries a caption and attribution. Simulation results are labeled as simulation.

legend.label: Demonstrated
legend.text: Shown working, with evidence linked here.

legend.label: Goal
legend.text: Planned or aspirational; not yet started or not guaranteed.

entries.title: Pilot build: Berkeley Humanoid Lite legs, standing
entries.text: At the University of Miami, undergraduate students Ahmed and Zara assembled Berkeley Humanoid Lite legs under Willie McClinton’s supervision. The prototype is standing; walking remains under development.
entries.framing: Reported pilot status from the course organizers. Photographs and test video will be added once documented.
entries.attribution: University of Miami pilot, supervised by Willie McClinton.

entries.title: Simulation: walking policy on the Berkeley Humanoid Lite model
entries.text: A reinforcement-learning walking policy (PPO) trained in MuJoCo on the Berkeley Humanoid Lite model, following a forward velocity command. The policy outputs joint-position targets at 50 Hz to a PD controller, the same interface a real motor driver exposes. Simulation only; no hardware result is implied.
entries.attribution: Simulation and video by Willie McClinton. Robot model: Berkeley Humanoid Lite (Hybrid Robotics, UC Berkeley), CC BY-SA 4.0.

media.alt: Simulated Berkeley Humanoid Lite walking forward on a checkered floor in MuJoCo.

entries.title: Simulation: standing policy on the Berkeley Humanoid Lite model
entries.text: A PPO standing policy trained in MuJoCo on the Berkeley Humanoid Lite model, using only observations a real robot can measure: IMU angular velocity, gravity direction, joint positions and velocities, and the previous action. This is the scaffolded setup the Week 3 assignment builds on. Simulation only.
entries.attribution: Simulation and video by Willie McClinton. Robot model: Berkeley Humanoid Lite (Hybrid Robotics, UC Berkeley), CC BY-SA 4.0.

media.alt: Simulated Berkeley Humanoid Lite standing upright on a checkered floor in MuJoCo.

entries.title: Next platform: a larger open humanoid around commercial actuators
entries.text: HBRN hardware contributors are designing a larger open humanoid built around commercial actuators as the platform that follows the course build. The work is at the simulation and design stage; nothing has been built yet, and it is not a course deliverable.

entries.title: Before January: validated lab sequence and prepared kits
entries.text: Before the course begins, the instructional team plans to validate the laboratory sequence, prepare components and spare parts, and test the software exercises. Actuator and limb builds, bench tests, and simulation checks will be documented here as they happen.

entries.title: Stretch goals: untethered walking and manipulation
entries.text: Successful untethered walking and manipulation are stretch goals for the final demonstrations, not promised outcomes. Final demonstrations will reflect validated hardware capabilities.

gallery.title: Simulation and render gallery
gallery.intro: Clips from the training scaffold the course assignments build on, rendered in MuJoCo, plus renders of the open hardware design. Everything here is simulation or CAD; no hardware result is implied.

items.title: Four open robots, one scaffold
items.caption: Walking policies trained with the same PPO pipeline on four open embodiments: Berkeley Humanoid Lite (top left), Asimov v0 legs (top right), Roboto Origin (bottom left), and an experimental composite of Asimov legs with the BHL torso (bottom right).
items.attribution: Simulation: Willie McClinton. Models: Berkeley Humanoid Lite (CC BY-SA 4.0), Asimov v0 by Asimov Inc (CERN-OHL-S 2.0), Roboto Origin by RoboParty (GPL-3.0).

items.title: Watching the motors work
items.caption: A walking policy on the Asimov v0 legs with every joint's torque shown as a share of its limit, the kind of readout students use to reason about actuator sizing.

media.alt: Simulated bipedal legs walking with a torque readout panel in the corner.
